newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit rebounds vs dollar on trade data.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit rebounds vs dollar on trade data.

text.p: The ringgit rebounded against the dollar on confirmation that Malaysia recorded a trade surplus of 600.7 million ringgit in August, dealers said.
The ringgit was earlier weakened by surging dollar/majors.

"The trade figure is going to set a bullish tone for the ringgit, because the government is expected to revise (down) its trade deficit forecast" in the 1997 budget presentation on Oct 25, said Jimmy Koh, an analyst at I.D.E.A.
At 0800 GMT, ringgit was at 2.5065/70 a dollar, after earlier trading as low as 2.5086.
The August data were in line with market expectations of a 500 million to 600 million surplus.
The ringgit's rebound was mild, keeping below its predicted resistance for the day at 2.5050 due to the strong dollar, dealers said.
"Dollar/yen remains biddish, which means it's a reasonable showing for ringgit," said a Malaysian bank dealer.
